title: SR2023 No1 lagoon/tank biogas methane-LDAR QA controls

sources.title: SR2023 No 1: capture, treatment and storage of biogas from lagoons and tanks
SR2023 No 1 generic risk assessment for capture, treatment and storage of biogas from lagoons and tanks

facts.source_fact: SR2023 No1 allows capture, treatment and storage of biogas from lagoons and tanks under the stated standard rules.
The rules allow upgrading biogas to biomethane at the place of production.
Upgraded biomethane may be injected into the national grid or used in vehicles at the place of production subject to the rules.
Auxiliary flares are limited to emergency, maintenance or protection of life and equipment conditions.
The permit does not allow combustion of biogas or biomethane in a spark engine for heat and power generation.
Combined biogas and biomethane collection and storage is limited to less than 10 tonnes.
Pressure systems must accommodate routine variation in gas flow, production and pressure events.
Gas pressures must be monitored and recorded.
Pressure-relief and vacuum systems must be inspected to ensure they are correctly seated.
Emissions of unburnt biogas must be minimised.
Methane leak detection, programmed routine maintenance inspections and repair must be carried out and recorded.
The rule states there shall be no point-source emissions to air, water or land.
If activities cause or are likely to cause pollution, the Environment Agency may require an emissions management plan.
An approved emissions management plan must be implemented from approval unless otherwise agreed.
The permit requires an LDAR programme for VOCs including methane with at least annual inspections.
The monitoring table specifies VOCs including methane monitoring every 6 months or as otherwise agreed under the LDAR programme.
Specified fugitive methane monitoring can use sniffing and/or Optical Gas Imaging techniques with BS EN 15446 and BS EN 17628.
A yearly LDAR summary report is required by 31 January.
Auxiliary flare use must be reported annually by 31 January, excluding short routine maintenance tests that remain documented.
The generic risk assessment recognises fugitive methane releases as contributing to long-term climate change risk.

guard_patterns.handling: Attach lagoon/tank capture and treatment scope.
Attach the current rule version and reporting periods.
Carry LDAR frequency, method and report provenance.
Do not convert facility controls to parcel emissions.
